#!/bin/bash
#
# docker-cleanup.sh
# Weekly Docker cleanup script to reclaim disk space by removing
# stopped containers, dangling/unused images, unused networks,
# unused volumes, and the build cache.
#
# Intended to be run by cron once a week.

set -u

LOG_DIR="/var/log/docker-cleanup"
LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/docker-cleanup.log"

mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}"

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*" >> "${LOG_FILE}"
}

log "===== Starting Docker cleanup ====="

# Make sure the docker CLI is available
if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "ERROR: docker command not found. Aborting."
    exit 1
fi

# Make sure the Docker daemon is reachable
if ! docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "ERROR: cannot talk to the Docker daemon. Aborting."
    exit 1
fi

log "Disk usage BEFORE cleanup:"
docker system df >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

# 1. Remove stopped containers
log "Removing stopped containers..."
docker container prune -f >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

# 2. Remove dangling and unused images (older than 7 days)
log "Removing unused images older than 7 days..."
docker image prune -a -f --filter "until=168h" >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

# 3. Remove unused networks
log "Removing unused networks..."
docker network prune -f >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

# 4. Remove unused volumes (careful: this drops data not attached to a container)
log "Removing unused volumes..."
docker volume prune -f >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

# 5. Clean build cache older than 7 days
log "Removing build cache older than 7 days..."
docker builder prune -a -f --filter "until=168h" >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

log "Disk usage AFTER cleanup:"
docker system df >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>&1

log "===== Docker cleanup finished ====="
exit 0

# Weekly Docker cleanup
# Runs every Sunday at 03:00 AM as root.
# Removes stopped containers, unused images/networks/volumes, and old build cache.
# Output is captured by the script itself in /var/log/docker-cleanup/docker-cleanup.log

SHELL=/bin/bash
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin

0 3 * * 0 root /app/scripts/docker-cleanup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1

# /etc/cron.d/docker-cleanup
#
# Weekly Docker cleanup
# Runs every Sunday at 03:00 AM as root.
# Removes stopped containers, unused images/networks/volumes, and old build cache.
# Output is captured by the script itself in /var/log/docker-cleanup/docker-cleanup.log

SHELL=/bin/bash
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin

0 3 * * 0 root /app/scripts/docker-cleanup.sh >/dev/null 2>&1

#!/bin/bash
#
# install.sh
# Installs the weekly Docker cleanup cron job.
# Must be run as root (or via sudo).

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "This installer must be run as root (try: sudo $0)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Installing Docker cleanup script..."
install -m 0755 -o root -g root \
    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/docker-cleanup.sh" /app/scripts/docker-cleanup.sh

echo "Installing cron job to /etc/cron.d/docker-cleanup..."
install -m 0644 -o root -g root \
    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/docker-cleanup.cron" /etc/cron.d/docker-cleanup

# /etc/cron.d entries must end with a newline and not be executable
chmod 0644 /etc/cron.d/docker-cleanup

echo "Creating log directory..."
mkdir -p /var/log/docker-cleanup
chmod 0755 /var/log/docker-cleanup

# Reload cron so it picks up the new file (works on most distros)
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    systemctl reload cron 2>/dev/null || systemctl reload crond 2>/dev/null || true
elif command -v service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    service cron reload 2>/dev/null || service crond reload 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "Done. The Docker cleanup will run every Sunday at 03:00 AM."
echo "Logs: /var/log/docker-cleanup/docker-cleanup.log"
echo "To run it manually now: sudo /app/scripts/docker-cleanup.sh"
